dedupe_keys.name: eplanopt multi objective evolutionary optimisation of energy scenarios coupling energyplan with deap eurac research

description: EPLANopt is an optimisation layer for the EnergyPLAN energy system model, developed by Eurac Research's Institute for Renewable Energy in Bolzano during its RegEnMod regional energy modelling project. The tool page read on 2026-09-28 explains that it couples EnergyPLAN, Aalborg University's hourly, sector-coupled simulation model, with a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm from the Python library DEAP to search capacity expansion options, returning sets of best future energy mixes that trade off several objectives, together with the cost structure of current and future systems, hourly energy flows and exchanges, and the measures that every good solution shares or avoids. The page says the code is published on a public GitLab repository under the GNU Lesser General Public License, with consultancy offered by Eurac. Coverage is not fixed: it applies to whatever system the EnergyPLAN model describes. Access is free under the LGPL; the repository itself was not opened. Caveats: it needs a working EnergyPLAN model of the system studied, and genetic searches can be slow. It supports capacity planning and optimisation studies, such as finding least-cost, low-carbon mixes of wind, solar, heat pumps and storage for a region by 2050. Related records: EnergyPLAN and the IDA Climate Response 2045 scenario built with it.
